assign.request: First test of a task mastermind started from a VS Code tab: prove a worktree, a commit on its own branch, and a report on the board. Task: handoff2.md items 2 and 3 — the fast assistant never promises a helper it has not started; helpers are started with the fast assistant as parent so their answers wake it.

assign.outcome:
**Two fast-assistant fixes, committed on their own branch and not merged.** Branch `worktree/helper-fixes`, commit `c598bbbb`, worktree `C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\helper-fixes`. Servex was not restarted, so the fixes go live only after a merge and a restart.

**1. No more promising a helper it has not started.** The cause was the assistant's own prompt (`Servex/agents/assistant.md`). It told the assistant to say "a helper is looking" in its reply, and that reply is posted before the code checks whether helpers are paused. Now the assistant never announces a helper. The code posts "A helper is looking into that now" only after one has really started, or the "paused" line when helpers are paused. It never posts both.

**2. Helpers report back to the assistant.** Each helper now starts with the fast assistant (`assistant-fast`) as its parent. When the helper finishes, Servex sends its answer to the assistant as well as posting it on the card. The prompt tells the assistant that such a message is for its own memory: it posts nothing, so you never see the answer twice. Helpers also end with their answer in a sentence or two, so that is what the assistant receives.

**Proof, without touching the live Servex.** A script loaded the worktree's code against a fake Servex. With helpers paused: no helper, one "paused" line. With helpers on: one helper started with parent `assistant-fast`, then one "looking" line. The real wake code delivered the helper's answer to `assistant-fast`. Both files pass `node --check`.

**Left.** Whether the model really stays silent on a helper's wake can only be seen live, after a merge and a Servex restart. `worktree-up.mjs` did not record this worktree in `.worktrees.json`, because my 90-second limit cut it off during boot. I stopped the spare dev server it had started.
